headline: Planning manager Sam Durfee presents RSA 79-E tax relief program for downtown and housing projects.
summary: The city has used the program only once, for the Cotton Mill project in 2013, which added 109 units. Relief can run up to seven years, and the board makes each decision after a public hearing; staff may bring a revised application to the board. Economic development director Liz Hannam also presented a skills gap analysis naming healthcare, retail, and manufacturing as top employers for residents. Her department has $70,000 for a $300,000 marketing plan.
discussion: RSA 79-E tax burden: Members asked whether other taxpayers cover the relief, and staff said an applicant-paid third-party review would show when new tax revenue covers service costs.

Skills gap data: Members questioned how the report counted commuters, including whether people who work in Merrimack count as leaving the city. Staff said the study cost $22,000 and used tax, GPS, and Census data.

Marketing plan funding: Staff said the $300,000 plan over 12 months has $70,000 in the budget, with up to $230,000 more possible through a supplemental appropriation or future budget. A member said the extra money does not appear likely.

Downtown retail hours: Members said many downtown shops close by 3:00 to 5:00 p.m. Staff said half of retail businesses do not stay open for the stroll and that the department is working with the Downtown Association.
